anchors.paper_title: How many people are able to control a P300-based brain–computer interface (BCI)?
anchors.reason: Guger et al. 2009 is a P300 BCI study of 100 subjects. This dataset has 10 subjects, a BrainAmp amplifier and Schreuder/Tangermann as authors, so it is topically related but not the data paper.

anchors.paper_title: Listen, You are Writing! Speeding up Online Spelling with a Dynamic Auditory BCI
anchors.reason: Same authors and auditory ERP speller topic, but this study has N=21 subjects. The dataset has 10 subjects and cites a different DOI (Neurosci Lett 2009), so it is not clearly this dataset's paper.

anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, used for dataset conversion, not a paper describing the BNCI 2015-003 P300 data.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard/specification used to format the dataset, not a paper describing this BNCI 2015-003 P300 dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Participants sat surrounded by six speakers at ear height (60° spacing, 65 cm radius). Each direction had a unique tone and band-pass filtered noise combination. EEG was recorded from 8 Ag/AgCl channels with a BrainAmp amplifier at 256 Hz, referenced to the nose. Session 1 consisted of calibration (48 trials) followed by online spelling with 15 fixed iterations. Session 2 consisted of calibration followed by online spelling with dynamic stopping (4-15 iterations). Classification used spatio-temporal features with a shrinkage-regularized linear binary classifier.
